text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Sweden's business commmunity has decided that Sweden should go the European economic and monetary union from the start in 1999. The state authorities are the main sceptics. This was according to a newspaper survey after the release of the report by an official government commission recommending a wait-and-see attitude.

- Capital gains saved Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo 1996 results. The company cashed in five percent of its shares in other companies during the year in a continuing divestment programme. Volvo posted a pre-tax and minorities profit of 14.20 billion crowns againt 13.06 billion in 1995. Sales of shares accounted for 8.27 billion crowns.
- Price falls in forestry product depressed the 1996 earnings of forestry group MoDo. Its profit fell 44 percent to 2.92 billion crowns.
- Ericsson employees in Norrkoping are worried about losing their jobs during a restructuring process. Up to 1,400 staff fear they could end up unemployed. A big demonstration is being held today.

- The government has proposed a law that will allow the government to cut off state sick benefits and other allowances if people refuse to let state employees inside their homes to check for abuse of the payments.

- Money is beginning to burn a hole in the pocket of Astra managing director Hakan Mogren. The Swedish drug company is one of the most profitable among major drug companies. It posted at 10 percent rise in 1996 profits on Wednesday.

- Redemption of a company's own shares is the trend among large Swedish companies this year. Volvo on Wednesday announced a share redemption scheme designed to give shareholders some of its surplus cash after a divestment programme.
- Mobile telephones are often useless in the train. The authority that owns the rails has decided to invest one billion crowns in a radio system that would improve this.

- Swedish drugs group Astra reported that pre-tax earnings for 1996 rose by 10 percent to 13.2 billion crowns. At the same time the board proposed a stock dividend of one new share for each three existing shares as well as a two for one stock split. Sales of ulcer medicine Losec climbed 15 percent.
- The Swedish National Police's list of foreign "mailbox" companies which are suspected of haivng swindled millions of crowns from Swedish investors has grown to 110 from 90 companies.

- Swedish industry picked up steam in December. The volume of new orders climbed by 3.3 percent to the highest level in a decade. Domestic orders were responsible for most of the rise. Statistics Sweden said new orders from the domestic market climbed 8.3 percent while export orders fell by 1.0 percent.

- Volvo was hurt last year by sharply decreased truck sales. It posted an operating profit of 3.7 billion crowns compared to 10.2 billion. Outgoing chief executive Soren Gyll said operating income was not at an acceptable level.
